# Source Map — INEGI ENOE 2022Q4 Technical Note (GOV-017, AMLO 2022, Ch.5B)

## Document frame
- **Type/role:** INEGI quarterly technical note for ENOE/ENOEN, Q4 2022. Official statistical body; results-bearing with methodological annex. Source role = official_statistical_body. (p.1, p.21)
- **Coverage:** Population 15+; national, 32 entidades federativas, 39 metropolitan areas, four locality-size strata. Probabilistic, two-stage, stratified, clustered design; five rotating panels. (p.21–p.22)
- **Comparability flags:** From Q3 2022 onward, **fieldwork returned to face-to-face only** (mixed phone+face-to-face during Q3 2020–Q2 2022). Pandemic-era PNEA-disponible classification ended Q3 2022 → revert to pre-pandemic criteria from Q3 2022 onward. Microdata back-rebuilt to Q1 2014 using new population estimate. ENOEN program concludes with Q4 2022; ENOE monthly+quarterly resumes with Jan-2023. (p.21, p.22–p.23, footnote * in p.3)
- **Seasonal adjustment:** X-13ARIMA-SEATS; adjusted and original series both reported. (p.23)

## Atomic claims (with locators; observed vs interpretive)

- **Observed (national, Q4 2022):** PEA 60.145 M; participation 60.4 % (vs 59.7 % Q4 2021, +0.8 pp). Occupied 58.349 M (97.0 % PEA, +0.7 pp); Unemployed 1.796 M (3.0 % PEA; women 3.1 %, men 2.9 %); long-term (>1 yr) unemployment 2.0 %. PNEA 39.370 M (39.6 %, –352 k). 32.157 M informal workers (TIL1 55.1 %, –0.7 pp). Suboccupation 4.4 M (7.5 %, –3.1 pp). TCCO 30.4 % of occupied (salario mínimo equivalente base Jan-2022; note slight definitional/salary-effect warning). (p.2–p.3 Cuadro 1; p.10; p.11 Cuadro 5; p.14 Cuadro 7; p.15–p.16 Cuadro 8)
- **Observed (sex distribution, Q4 2022):** PEA men 35.746 M (76.5 %), women 24.400 M (46.2 %; +1.6 pp y/y). Women in informal sector +736 k y/y; men –188 k. (p.2, p.11 Cuadro 5)
- **Observed (sector, Q4 2022):** Tertiary 62.7 %; Secondary 24.9 %; Primary 11.8 %. Comercio +279 k; manufacturing +260 k; servicios diversos +201 k; restaurantes/alojamiento +217 k. (p.6, p.8 Cuadro 3)
- **Observed (subordinate wage workers, Q4 2022):** 39.775 M (68.2 %). Health-care access 56.9 % (+1.1 M y/y); written contract 22.863 M; without contract 16.302 M; ≤1 minimum wage 11.094 M; 1–2× minimum wage 16.003 M. (p.9 Cuadro 4)
- **Observed (locality-size, Q4 2022):** Urban-high ≥100 k residents hosts 49.5 % of occupied; rural <2.5 k hosts 20.4 %; urban-low 14.7 %; urban-mid 15.4 %. Unemployment rate higher in larger localities (3.6 % vs 1.7 % rural). (p.4–p.5 Cuadro 2; p.12 Cuadro 6)
- **Observed (seasonally adjusted, q/q):** Unemployment 3.1 % (–0.1 pp); TIL1 –0.4 pp; TOSI1 –0.2 pp; suboccupation rate –0.1 pp. (p.10, p.11, p.14)
- **Observed (state dispersion, Q4 2022):** Highest participation BCS 69.2 %, CDMX 62.6 %. Highest unemployment CDMX/Edomex 4.5 %, Tabasco 4.2 %. Highest informality Oaxaca 81.2 %, Guerrero 79 %, Chiapas 75.2 %. Lowest informal Coahuila 34.2 %, Nuevo León 35.8 %. Highest TCCO Chiapas 48.1 %; lowest Jalisco 15.1 %. (p.16–p.17, Cuadro 9)
- **Observed (39-city aggregate, Q4 2022):** Participation 61.6 %; unemployment 3.7 %; suboccupation 7.2 %; TCCO 26.2 %; TIL1 43.5 %. 64 % of occupied concentrated in 8 metro areas. (p.19, Cuadro 10)

## Methodology and limitations carried forward
- **Comparable series only via salario mínimo equivalente base ene-2022** for income-classified rates (TCCO, TIL). INEGI publishes comparable series online. (p.9 footnote 1; p.15; p.16 Gráfica 6 note)
- **Pandemic classification change** (PNEA-disponible incl. temporales con vínculo + желающих trabajar) operated Q3-2020 → Q2-2022; **discontinued** from Q3-2022 — structural break for some PNEA components relative to earlier quarters. (p.3 fn *; p.22–p.23)
- **Field mode:** phone+face-to-face mixed Q3-2020 → Q2-2022; **face-to-face only** from Q3-2022 onward — another structural break. (p.21)
- **No sampling error, CVs, or confidence intervals reported in this note**; only point estimates with y/y and q/q differences. Note 5 (p.19) only validates metro-area inclusion for state-level comparability.
- **Document does not assert causality, intent, or competency attribution** to government policy; contains no policy-evaluation language.

## Skeptical/policy-critical angles supported by the text
- National averages mask deep regional gaps in informality (Oaxaca 81.2 % vs Coahuila 34.2 %) and TCCO (Chiapas 48.1 % vs Jalisco 15.1 %). (p.16–p.17, Cuadro 9)
- Aggregate unemployment and participation improved y/y, but **27 % of occupied still worked >48 h/week** and **6.2 % <15 h**; **22.6 % self-employed without employees**; **42.0 % of subordinate workers without written contract**; **16.8 M without health-care access through work**. (Cuadros 3, 4, 7)
- Tasa de Ocupación Parcial y Desocupación (TOPD1) 9.0 % — higher for women (12.6 %). (Cuadro 8)
- Time-of-unemployment longer than 3 months fell to 15.2 % but absolute counts of long-duration unemployment reduced meaningfully (>3 mo –341 k, >6 mo –76 k). (p.13–p.14)

## Sections a stronger reviewer should reopen
- Verify whether Q3-2022 PNEA reclassification affects the y/y comparison for PNEA-disponible (–2.071 M) and PNEA-no-disponible (+1.719 M) — partly mechanical. (p.3 Cuadro 1, fn *)
- Verify survey-mode break (phone→face-to-face) impact on response rate and any nonresponse bias for Q4-2022 vs Q4-2021 (note is silent on response rates/CV).
- Confirm whether salario-mínimo-equivalente adjustments are already baked into reported TCCO or only available on INEGI's separate tabulados.

## Caveats / traps honoured
- No inference of AMLO/government motive or causation. Headline figures are point estimates; sampling error not disclosed here.
- Quarter-to-quarter movements attributed by INEGI to seasonal adjustment, not to real economic regime change.
- All unit/percentage assertions reproduced verbatim from Cuadros 1, 3, 5, 7, 8, 9, 10 with page locators; no fabrication.

*(Source map prepared per Ch.5B evidence-reader protocol; no scoring performed.)*
